subject: [Escalation] RetryWave causing 504s/429s — HitSilver production impact
messages:
From: Sara Holden <sara@hitsilver.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production 504/429 spike — retry wave impacting inference calls

Jasmine / Monica,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 504s and 429s from Redwood starting ~07:45 PT this morning. Our service is surface-level: high-level call volume is steady, but the downstream error rate is spiking and our front-end is triggering aggressive retries. The result: session timeouts and elevated latencies for user-facing features.

Symptoms:
- 504 surge across inference endpoints between 07:45–08:05 PT (peaked at ~18% error rate)
- 429 bursts coincident with client-side retries
- Significant tail latency (p95 -> ~4.6s) causing our retry logic to cascade

We rely on Redwood Dedicated (us-west) with your default batching + KV prefix caching. Can you confirm whether any changes were deployed or if there are known cache/batching regressions? We need an ETA for mitigation — this is impacting paying users.

I attached an aggregated request log and a short trace. Happy to hop on a quick call.

--
Sara Holden
Head of Integrations, HitSilver
sara@hitsilver.ai

Date: 2026-11-15T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production 504/429 spike — retry wave impacting inference calls

Quick technical summary from triage (logs attached):

Findings so far:
- No deliberate deploys to runtime in us-west within the window. There was a config rollout to the batching controller yesterday but it targeted canaries only.
- We are seeing a KV-cache mutation pattern where a small subset of prefixes are being over-evicted. Evictions are causing cache miss storms; misses increase backend pressure which lengthens queueing time, pushing requests past our L7 gateway timeout (504).
- A separate observation: a shard rebalance triggered an uneven hot-key distribution (one worker got ~60% of a high-volume prefix). That worker's request queue filled and started returning 504s; client retry logic amplified the load (retry wave).

Immediate mitigations applied (09:00–09:15 PT):
1) Decreased max_batch_size from 64 -> 24 on us-west serving pool.
2) Temporarily disabled aggressive prefix rebalancing (falls back to stable mapping).
3) Tightened kv-cache eviction threshold to conservative mode (reduce thrash).
4) Applied an emergency route-policy to split HitSilver traffic across a secondary pool in us-east (warm fallback) to relieve the hot shard.

Preliminary impact: aggregate 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 6% within 10 minutes, p95 latency improved ~30%. Still monitoring for residual retry amplification.

Attached: diagnostic_trace_20261115.txt (key traces), hitsilver_request_logs_20261115.tar.gz (aggregated request ids).

-Monica
Lead Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: [Exec brief] HitSilver production incident — retry wave and KV-cache hot-shard (summary + next steps)

Team / Sara, quick exec summary for leadership / customer execs: 

What happened (tl;dr):
HitSilver experienced a production outage window on 2026-11-15 triggered by a hot-prefix causing excessive KV-cache evictions and a shard imbalance. That produced a cascade of cache-miss load onto a single worker, increasing queueing and leading to 504s. Aggressive client retries created a retry wave that amplified backend pressure and produced 429/504 spikes.

Impact: 
- Customer-visible 504/429 spikes between ~07:45–09:20 PT. Peak error rate ~18%.
- HitSilver reported session timeouts and degraded user experience. No data loss reported.

Immediate mitigations performed: 
- Reduced max batch size and disabled aggressive prefix rebalancing in us-west.
- Tightened cache eviction settings to stop thrash.
- Rerouted a portion of traffic to a warm fallback pool in us-east.
- Result: error rate reduced to ~4–6% and p95 latency improved by ~30% within an hour.

Root cause (preliminary):
- A shard rebalance + a high-volume prefix produced uneven hot-key load on a single worker while a recent canary update to our batching controller made that worker more sensitive to load. The combination triggered evictions and queueing beyond gateway timeout thresholds.

Next steps / RCA timeline:
1) Marcus will deliver a full RCA with timeline and reproduction steps by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-16).
2) Engineering will revert the canary config in the batching controller and create a safer rollout guard (progressive rollout + short-circuit on hot-key detection).
3) Product/Customer Success will coordinate a post-mortem call with HitSilver; Jasmine will draft a customer-facing summary and proposed credits/credits policy.

Customer ask and commercial note:
- HitSilver requested an update on potential credit/contract remediation; will discuss post-RCA. Jordan/Sales team — please advise on commercial.

Attachments: diagnostic_trace_20261115.txt, hitsilver_request_logs_20261115.tar.gz

-Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
